FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on Bulk Handling Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee and approval Engineering Division Council. the recommendations of of the Heavy Mechanical

This Indian Standard covers the general requirements of electronic type bagging machines. requirements laid down in the Indian Standard are not withstanding the requirements of any Status, Regulations, Acts and Rules or any other Central or State Governments Orders issued time to time which are otherwise to be met.

The other from

Electronic type bagging machines are taking the place of mechanical type bagging machines where feasible. This Indian Standard therefore, attempts to provide uniform guidelines to the purchaser This standard covers a net-weigher type and the supplier on the electronic type bagging machines. bagging machines (electronic ) suitable for filling in open mouthed and/or valve type bags. Taring The data sheet necessary for of bags is also possible as soon as the bag is put on the machine. selection and design of these type of bagging machine -have been laid down in IS 13945 : 1994 `Bulk handling equipment - Bagging machines ( Electronic type ) - Data sheet'. The general requirements for design and construction of mechanical type bagging been specified in IS 13989 : 1994 `Bulk handling equipment - Bagging machines type ) - Design and construction - General requirements'. In the preparation of this standard issued by Organization lnternationale OTML C 8 Non-automatic OTML R 60 Metrological OIML OIML OIML R 61 Automatic R 74 Electronic R 87 Net content assistance has been De Metrologie Legale: instruments for load cell filling machines instruments derived from the following machine have ( Mechanical

Accuracy requirements have been specified in International Recommendation OIML R 61. Accuracies other than those specified in 4.6 may be adopted as per agreement between purchaser and the manufacturer. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1963 `Rules for rounding off `numerical values ( revised 1'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
